why_it_matters: Working out how much fabric a triangle flag or a pennant needs, without buying twice as much as you use.

concepts.text: Two identical triangles fit together to make a rectangle (or a parallelogram)
A rectangle's area is base × height
So one triangle is half of that rectangle: area = ½ × base × height

misconception: Area of a triangle is base times height, so a 6 by 4 triangle is 24

boss.name: Duke Doublecount
boss.backstory: A peacock in a tiny cape who carries a sign reading '△ = b × h' and claims the whole rectangle every time he sees half of one.

taunt: I have counted the entire rectangle. You are welcome.
Halves are for creatures with smaller signs.
heal: Excellent. Base times height. Write that on everything.
hit: This is most irregular. Kindly stop folding my rectangle.
I did not authorize a second triangle.
lines.ko: I object to being divided by two.

cliffhanger: I heard a parallelogram is base × height too. Even the slanted ones? That can't be right… right?

quiz.question: A triangle has base 6 and height 4. Put two copies of it together. What shape can they make, and what are its base and height?
quiz.answer: A rectangle (or a parallelogram) with base 6 and height 4.

quiz.question: What is the area of a rectangle with base 10 and height 5?
A right triangle has a base of 10 and a height of 5. What is its area?
quiz.answer: 25 square units (10 × 5 ÷ 2): it is half of a 10 by 5 rectangle.
